solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Oval tie clip with large split

indicators.note: something split is broken apart, so the letters are pulled to pieces and reassembled

parts.note: L is the standard clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A tie clip shaped like an oval has broken in two because it was so large.
explanation.definitionFit: Elliptic is the geometric adjective for something shaped like an ellipse, an oval outline.

clue.text: Provide income now or tomorrow — somehow, all do

parts.words: now or tomorrow — somehow, all do
parts.note: the three words now, tomorrow and somehow all finish with the same two letters, O and W

explanation.surface: Funding is promised now or later, and somehow everybody gets it.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer three and two: what the three words all do is finish in OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give money that supplies a lasting income, as a college endowment does.

clue.text: Ill-advised Danish coppers caught following pimp having blown cover

indicators.note: the police and caught letters come after what is left of pimp
the word pimp loses its covering outer letters

parts.note: politi is the Danish word for police
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Danish police arrested a pimp whose cover was blown, an unwise move.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolitic actions are unwise and tactless, lacking good judgement.

clue.text: Journey over, left island capital

parts.note: a trip is a journey
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A trip is finished and an island capital is left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: Women, long-mocked, treated badly — it'll hardly surprise you

indicators.note: letters abused and knocked about are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women have long been mocked and mistreated, as no one will be surprised to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts everybody already knows cannot astonish anyone, so they come as no surprise.

clue.text: Bond agent, outwardly macho, stripped off after introduction to Tiffany

indicators.note: the stripped macho letters come after the Tiffany letter
only the outside letters of the word agent are kept
the introduction to a name is its opening letter
the word macho has its outer letters peeled away like clothing, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: James Bond, the secret agent, is macho until he strips off after meeting a woman called Tiffany, as in Diamonds Are Forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' gives AT from agent; 'stripped off' leaves ACH from macho; 'introduction to' gives T. 'Bond' looks like 007 but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bond things is to fix or join them together, the same as fastening one to another.

clue.text: Going round university, almost all male students graduate

indicators.note: the shortened all and the male letter surround the university letter
the word all loses its last letter

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Nearly every male student at the university graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a former student who has graduated from a school or university.

clue.text: Leader of action group working for freedom

indicators.note: the first letter of the word action

parts.note: a band is a group
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A leader of an activist group campaigning for liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with abandon means with complete lack of restraint, uninhibited liberty.

clue.text: Prevented top news boss literally escaping?

parts.note: head means top
ED is short for editor, the boss at a newspaper
off means getting away, departing

explanation.surface: A newspaper's top editor is literally on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: To head someone off is to intercept and block them, stopping them in advance.

clue.text: Old city, part of Pennsylvania's best-known metropolis

indicators.note: only a stretch from inside the name of the city is used, the rest dropped

parts.note: Philadelphia is the largest city in Pennsylvania

explanation.surface: A historic city that forms part of Philadelphia, Pennsylvania's famous metropolis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes six consecutive letters from PHILADELPHIA, a word not printed in the clue, dropping PHILA in front and A behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi was an ancient Greek city, home of the oracle of Apollo.

clue.text: Most of light dish otherwise called a casserole

indicators.note: all but the final letter of the dish is kept

parts.note: a mousse is a light, airy dish
aka is the abbreviation for 'also known as'

explanation.surface: A light dish that might also be described as a casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: Moussaka is a Greek baked dish of layered aubergine and minced meat, a kind of casserole.

clue.text: Rich, boring person's memo to self?

definitions.meaning: someone who bores holes in the ground would note a well on their list of things to do

explanation.surface: A wealthy but dull person writing themselves a reminder note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull but means drilling; a driller's to-do item is a well.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-off people are comfortably prosperous, which is exactly what rich means.

clue.text: Sons standing down from unnecessary rivalry

indicators.note: the sons withdraw, so their letters leave the word

parts.note: needless means unnecessary
S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons are SS

explanation.surface: Two sons retire from a pointless family feud.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle in British sport means bad feeling or keen rivalry between opponents, as in a needle match.

clue.text: Crime study by John

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over, as in conning a text
a john is a prostitute's client, also called a trick

explanation.surface: A criminology study written by someone called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name; it is slang for a prostitute's customer, which is also a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle in which someone is deceived out of money is a criminal act.

clue.text: New brochure on good port

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A fresh travel brochure promoting a fine harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherbourg is a French ferry port on the Normandy coast.

clue.text: Brief display about international religion

indicators.note: the shortened display goes about, around, the international letters
cut short, so the last letter of the word for display goes

parts.note: a show is a display

explanation.surface: A short exhibition about a world faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the traditional nature and ancestor-worshipping faith of Japan.

clue.text: Senseless, self-inflicted problem, one dividing two US states

indicators.note: the own goal and one split the two state abbreviations apart

parts.note: ILL abbreviates Illinois and CAL California
OG is an own goal in football, a self-inflicted blunder
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pointless self-made problem causing a rift between two American states.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical lacks reason, which is what senseless means.

clue.text: Previous bills or demands

parts.note: ex means former, previous
a bill passed by Parliament becomes an act

explanation.surface: Earlier invoices or payment demands.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact something is to demand and obtain it, as in exacting payment or revenge.

clue.text: Answer question over Arabs once Iraq regularly reveals tanks

parts.note: AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: every other letter of the word Iraq is taken

explanation.surface: An answer to a question about Arabs once living in Iraq reveals tanks, as in war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanks' suggests military vehicles in Iraq; they are fish tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks for keeping fish, the plural of aquarium.

clue.text: Little chap should hold line soon

indicators.note: the line letter is held inside the little chap

parts.note: shorty is a nickname for a short man

explanation.surface: A small man ought to be keeping his place in the queue soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly means before long, in a little while.

clue.text: Finished a tiny jumper, following to the end where extra instructions might be found?

definitions.text: where extra instructions might be found?

parts.note: over means finished

indicators.note: the following letter is shifted to the end of the jumper's word

parts.note: a flea is a tiny jumping insect
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Knitting pattern: once a small sweater is completed, further instructions continue on the next page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater (a knitting pattern), but it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuation instructions are printed on the other side of the page, the reverse of the sheet.

clue.text: Very strict communication unopened by soldiers

indicators.note: the communication loses its first letter

parts.note: a text is a phone message
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: An unopened message from soldiers sent under very strict conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme measures are the harshest, most severe, utterly rigorous ones.

clue.text: Unlimited strikes interrupting House led by British Prime Minister

indicators.note: the British letter comes first
the trimmed strikes break into the house letters
without its limits, first and last letters

parts.note: butts are blows with the head, strikes

explanation.surface: Endless industrial action disrupting Parliament, under a British Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlimited' trims BUTTS to UTT. 'British Prime Minister' tempts a UK name, but the PM is Pakistan's.
explanation.definitionFit: Benazir Bhutto, and her father Zulfikar, both served as Prime Minister of Pakistan.

clue.text: Burning, single and dashing, all out to get engaged in a suit

parts.note: lit means alight, burning
I is the Roman numeral one, single

indicators.note: the word all goes out of the word for dashing

parts.note: gallant means dashing, chivalrous

explanation.surface: A passionate, unattached, dashing man goes all out to become engaged to be married in a suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' and 'suit' evoke a wedding; here the suit is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigant as an adjective describes a party taking part in a lawsuit.

clue.text: People in general blocking an offensive brief message

indicators.note: the people letters sit in the way, inside the offensive

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 Vietnam War campaign
we can mean people in general

explanation.surface: The public prevent a rude short message from appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as rude but is the military campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on Twitter, now X.

clue.text: Rebelling and still moved forcibly

parts.note: up means in revolt, as in up in arms
rooted to the spot means motionless, still

explanation.surface: Rebels who stood their ground were nonetheless forcibly displaced.
explanation.definitionFit: People uprooted are forced from their homes, displaced against their will.

clue.text: Flight south, having been stuck in city — take off

indicators.note: the south letter is stuck inside the city letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
to ape is to imitate, take off

explanation.surface: A flight heading south after being stranded in a city, ready to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like an aircraft departing; it means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight in the sense of running away from danger is a getaway.

clue.text: Right to stop lame award

indicators.note: the right letter plugs, stops, the word for lame

parts.note: gammy is British slang for a lame or injured leg

explanation.surface: Somebody must step in to halt a feeble prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grammys are annual American music industry awards.

clue.text: Agreed to intercept mobilised fleet's command for port observation?

indicators.note: the agreement word cuts into the rearranged fleet
the fleet is set in motion, its letters moved around

parts.note: the word fleet is the fodder; the apostrophe-s is a possessive serving the surface only
yes signals agreement

explanation.surface: Consent given to stop a navy's order to keep watch from harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobilised' turns FLEET into E-LEFT for YES to split. 'port' is not a harbour but the nautical left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade-ground order to turn the head to the left, port being the nautical left.
